chunks: Do not set up another god with God, or you will remain disgraced and destitute.
ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of setting up another god with Allah?
ai.summary: This verse, situated within Surah Al-Isra, serves as a foundational injunction for Tawhid, warning that associating partners with Allah (Shirk) leads to both social disgrace (mardhum) and divine abandonment (makhdhul). In Shia scholarly tradition, this is often interpreted not merely as a theological statement but as a practical guide for maintaining spiritual integrity and avoiding the loss of divine support in worldly and otherworldly affairs. The dual consequence highlights the immediate and ultimate costs of deviating from pure monotheism.
